title: Rehearsing We — what would it take for us to have a real say over the things we depend on?

fragments.text: At work they put next week's shifts up on Friday. I've got to sort out childcare before that. I've asked the manager twice and she says it's the system, but someone chose that system, didn't they?
A few of us want the rota two weeks ahead. I think they'd listen if we asked together. But I'm on extra hours at the moment and I need them. I don't want to be the person who gets their shifts cut.
I'd be happy for someone to talk to the manager for us. I can't go to meetings all the time. I just want them to check with us before saying we've agreed to something.

There's damp in my flat and the letting agent keeps telling me to open the windows. Then I found out the people upstairs have the same problem. Until we actually spoke, I thought it was just me getting fobbed off.

We could put all the repair requests in one email and copy everyone in. That's something I would do. People keep saying we should all stop paying rent, but I don't know what happens after that. I can't risk having to move again.
If we get someone to speak for the building, it shouldn't just be whoever talks most in the group chat. There's a woman downstairs who doesn't use it. She still needs to be asked.

They've cut the evening bus where I live. I can get to my dad's, but I can't get home afterwards unless I pay for a taxi. There was a consultation, apparently. I only heard about it once they'd decided.

We sent a petition about the bus and got a polite reply. I don't know what we're meant to do next. People suggest boycotting it, but we're the ones who need it. How do you put pressure on someone when you can't just walk away?

I don't really want to run a bus service with my neighbours. I want the people whose job it is to run it to answer to us. I'd help collect people's journeys and go to a meeting. I don't want that becoming another unpaid job.

Our school moved the after-school club to a different site. They said most parents were happy with it. Nobody asked me, and it adds half an hour to my day. I would have liked a say before they booked everything.

We did get them to change the collection time once. A few parents got together and showed how many people couldn't make it. So it can work. It was mostly two mums chasing everyone, though, and one of them has had enough now.

Everyone says we should share the work. Fine, but which work? If you're asking me to make phone calls, say how many and by when. I can do a couple. I can't agree to be available whenever something comes up.

I do deliveries and the app changed what it pays for longer trips. There wasn't anyone to ask about it. I just got a notification. I don't even know most of the other riders, so I wouldn't know where to start.

If enough of us logged off at the same time, maybe they'd notice. But people need the money that day. Could we put some money aside to cover that? I like the idea, but I haven't got much spare either.

I'd want to know who can take money out of a shared fund. I don't need to vote on every little thing, but I do want to see where it's gone. And who decides if somebody needs help more than somebody else?

I live in a housing co-op, so we do get a vote. That's good, but the same three people have been on the committee for years. When I asked about the service charges, they sent me a spreadsheet I couldn't understand.

We replaced our cleaning company after people kept complaining, and it's better now. We could actually change the contract. But I'm not convinced voting on everything is the answer. Choosing someone to fix the boiler took us weeks.
I'd let someone who knows about boilers choose the contractor, within a budget we agree. If they do a bad job, we need a way to replace them. I don't want another three meetings about pipework.

My mum's care visits keep changing time, and I end up filling the gaps. When I phone, I get passed between the council and the company. I want to know who's actually able to change it, because everyone says it isn't them.

Other families must be dealing with this too. I'd like us to compare what's happening. But please don't make the answer that we should all take turns doing the care ourselves. I'm already doing more than I can manage.
I could come to a meeting if someone stayed with my mum. That's the sort of help I'd need. Sending me more information doesn't give me another free evening.

I joined a local campaign to stop the library hours being cut. There were loads of messages, but I couldn't work out who was deciding what we'd do. After a while I stopped reading them. I still wanted the library open.

I don't think we all have to agree about everything to do one thing together. I'd help with the library even if I didn't like someone's politics. But I would want to know what we were actually asking for before putting my name on it.

I'd give it another go if there was a specific job and I could see what happened afterwards. Even if we lost, just tell us. Last time it all went quiet and I never found out whether anyone had met the council.
